sentences.text: Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court may think just and proper may also kindly be allowed in the interest of justice."

3. The petitioners, who are the husband, brother-in-law (jeth), co-sister (jethani), father-in-law and mother-in-law, respectively of the respondent No.2, have filed this petition under Section 528 of the BNSS 2023 stating therein that the marriage between the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was solemnised on 11.12.2021 at Durg.

An F.I.R. bearing registration No. 42/2022 came to be registered with P.S. Mahila Thana, Durg, District Durg (C.G.) against the petitioners herein for the offences punishable u/s 498-A/34 of I.P.C. r/w section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
As per the averment of the F.I.R. the respondent no.2 is living in her matrimonial house since 16.03.2022.

The respondent no.2 has filed the criminal complaint against the husband and his relatives under section 498A r/w 34 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act alleging cruelty and harassment for demand of dowry and misappropriation of ornaments and money.
It is also alleged that the respondent no.2 was subjected to mental and physical torture by the present petitioners.
Upon receiving the complaint the Mahila police Thana Durg had registered the present Crime against the petitioners and after registration of an F.I.R. the criminal law was set on motion.
The local police on completion of the investigation filed its final report before Judicial Magistrate First.

4. At the very outset learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties on 5.7.2025 and thereafter they moved an application seeking closure of criminal case on the ground of amicable settlement between both of them.
The said fact is evident from the order sheet dated 5-7-2025 (page 85 of the petition).
The compromise deed dated 05.07.2025 is annexed with the present petition.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent No. 2 has admitted the fact of compromise and he has no objection.
